<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bonded Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=762) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Downtime" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=49" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 259

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

You forge strong connections with animals. You can spend 7 days of downtime regularly interacting with a normal animal (not a companion or other special animal) that is friendly or helpful to you. After this duration, attempt a DC 20 [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=22) check. If successful, you bond with the animal. The animal is permanently [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21) to you, unless you do something egregious to break your bond. A helpful animal is easier to direct, as described under [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58).

 Bonding with a new animal ends any previous bond you had. You can't have both a bonded animal and an animal companion (though you can have both a bonded animal and a familiar).

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bonds of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3489) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 35

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486)

**Requirements**
You have cast [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666) this turn.

</column>

---

You sway with the motions of your spells that animate the dead, channeling your power to sustain two at the same time. You Sustain your previous casting of _animate dead_, binding the necromantic energy of the two spells together with metaphysical twine. On subsequent rounds, you can Sustain both _animate dead_ spells with a single action to Sustain the Spell. This benefit lasts until either of the spells ends.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bone Burst](/Feats.aspx?ID=9116) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 35

**Trigger**
A creature adjacent to one of your thralls uses a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) action or a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action, makes a ranged [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540), or leaves a square during a move action it’s using, and you are within 30 feet of the thrall.

</column>

---

You destroy the thrall in an explosion of bone shards that fly toward the triggering creature, dealing 2d10 piercing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your spell DC. 

The damage increases to 3d10 at 12th and to 4d10 at 18th level.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bone Caller](/Feats.aspx?ID=2409) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=226" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 47

</column>

---

Using a mixture of dinosaur bones and the bones of your ancestors to focus your magic, you animate lizards and dinosaurs to carry messages or serve as mounts. You can cast [_animal messenger_](/Spells.aspx?ID=11) and [_phantom steed_](/Spells.aspx?ID=221) as primal innate spells once per day each. The animal messenger is always a Tiny dinosaur or lizard, and your innate spell transforms it from bones to flesh, even if there are no dinosaurs or lizards nearby. The _phantom steed_ looks like a dinosaur rather than a horse but functions identically.

You can remove your ribs to use them as arrows or bolts. When you draw a rib, you lose 2 HP, and the projectile deals 2 extra negative damage if you Strike with it before the end of your next turn. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bone Speaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=9098) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 33

</column>

---

To truly understand the mechanical advantages of an undead skeleton, you must understand how it functioned in life. You can [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) on living creatures with an internal or external skeleton using [Undead Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you do, you can learn only information pertaining to the biology of a creature—not any learned abilities or abilities granted by items.

Additionally, you can perform a forensic examination on a corpse using Undead Lore instead of [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) if the corpse came from a creature with a skeleton.

For 1 minute, you can make bone spike [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strikes, which deal 1d6 piercing damage and have the [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) and [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194) trails. When you take the Bone Spikes action, you can choose one weapon on your person and duplicate its weapon runes onto your bone spikes (with the exception of any runes that couldn't apply to the bone spears).

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 57 **Frequency** once per day --- You scatter your body and transform into a whirling storm of bones for up to 1 minute or until you spend a single action to return to your normal shape. You become Huge, gain the [swarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=239) trait, and gain a fly Speed of 40 feet. As a swarm, you have the following characteristics.
  • You are immune to the [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), and [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) conditions.
  • You have weakness 5 to area and [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage.
  • You can occupy the same space as other creatures and must do so to use your damaging ability.
  • As a 2-action activity, you can deal 10d6 bludgeoning damage to all creatures sharing your space ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save with a DC equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher).
  • You can't speak, Cast Spells, use [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) actions requiring your hands, Activate magic items, or make any Strikes with your normal body.
  • You don't gain the [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=36) ability, so you are still affected normally by [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects. You also retain the benefits of skeleton feats that don't require communication or the use of hands.

Whenever an enemy starts its turn adjacent to you, it must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is highest. On a failure, the enemy takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls and skill checks for as long as it remains adjacent to you. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is then temporarily immune to bonekeeper's bane for 24 hours.

Before your soul returned to the Material Plane, you interacted with a host of other souls on their way to the Boneyard. One of these acquaintances owes you a favor. You can temporarily summon it to come to your aid, and it appears as a swirling mass of ectoplasm with indiscernible features and a translucent dagger, the favored weapon of Pharasma. You have a powerful connection to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15) and its courts, granting you the ability to travel to and from the Boneyard. You gain [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) as a divine innate spell. You can cast it twice per week. ---

You aren't satisfied with keeping to just one kind of boost from your constant tinkering, so you've learned to modulate between several possibilities at once. Choose two additional [offensive boosts](/Classes.aspx?ID=19). You can use an Interact action to change the offensive boost currently affecting your weapon, choosing between the one you chose for the class feature and the two you chose for this modification. If your weapon has the [modular](/Traits.aspx?ID=271) trait, you can swap the offensive boost as part of the Interact action you take to use that trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187)

**Prerequisites**
[Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807)

</column>

---

Knowing how someone thinks makes it much easier to know where they'll be, or even replace them altogether. You can cast [_mind probe_](/Spells.aspx?ID=193) as an innate occult spell once per day, using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

 If you cast _mind probe_ on a target you're studying for the purpose of Assuming their Role, and the target fails their save, you can delay the spell from coming into effect until you Assume their Role. When you use the spell this way, you can Sustain it up to 10 times during its duration, asking a question each time. The spell lasts until you ask all 10 questions or are no longer Assuming the Role, whichever comes first. You don't need to Sustain the Spell to extend its duration—only when asking a question—nor do you need to be in range or have line of effect to Sustain it.

May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers **Source** [Gatewalkers Player's Guide (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=287) pg. 11 --- Your touch opens a conduit into the mind of your target, the emptiness within you pulling skills and memories through. You touch an adjacent creature and choose any skill you believe they are trained or better in. If you choose a skill that they are trained or better in, you borrow their proficiency in that skill, becoming trained in that skill for 1 minute. If they are not trained in the skill you choose, the GM chooses the next most applicable skill (for instance, choosing [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) instead of [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)). At 12th level, you can become an expert in the skill if the target is as well. If the target of Borrowed Ability is unwilling, the effects depend on the target’s Will save. **Critical Success** The target resists your touch completely.
**Success** Your borrowing is unstable. At the beginning of each of your turns, you must either relinquish your hold on the borrowed skill (as a free action), or attempt another backlash check for your deviation; the ability ends if you fail.
**Failure** Borrowed Ability lasts for its full duration.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 44

**Prerequisites**
[Rock Runner](/Feats.aspx?ID=4391)

</column>

---

Your dwarven build allows you to push foes around, just like a mighty boulder tumbles through a subterranean cavern. Take a [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=87) into the square of a foe that is your size or smaller, and the foe must move into the empty space directly behind it. The foe must move even if doing so places it in harm's way. The foe can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) DC to block your Step. If the foe attempts this saving throw, it takes bludgeoning damage equal to your level plus your Strength modifier unless it critically succeeds.

If the foe can't move into an empty space (if it is surrounded by solid objects or other creatures, for example), your Boulder Roll has no effect.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tripkee" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=793" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 21

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)

**Trigger**
An adjacent ally attempts to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378).

</column>

---

You’ve learned to use your own athletic abilities and springy legs to help others who need a boost with their leaps. The triggering ally gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378). This bonus increases to +2 if you’re an expert in Athletics, +3 if you’re a master, and +4 if you’re legendary. Additionally, the triggering ally’s [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) distance on a successful check increases by 2 feet for a High Jump or 5 feet for a Long Jump, even if it would allow the ally to Leap further than their land Speed.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bound in Ice](/Feats.aspx?ID=3419) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 11

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
[Frostbite Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3417)

</column>

---

You become a hybrid of your ancestry and a saumen kar. Your size increases to Large, and your reach becomes 10 feet. Your [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) resistance increases to be equal to your level, and you gain [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) resistance equal to half your level.

 You also gain the Blizzard Evasion reaction.

 **Blizzard Evasion** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You take 40 or more physical damage from a single attack; **Effect** You discorporate into a whirling blizzard for up to 3 rounds. During this time, you gain resistance 10 to physical damage and weakness 10 to [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) damage. You gain a fly speed of 40 feet, but the only action you can take is to [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94). The first time each round you enter another creature's space while discorporated, or the first time a creature enters your space, that creature takes 4d8 cold damage and must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or else be [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). At the start of your turn, you can end this effect as a free action.

---

When focused on finding your quarry, you're relentless. You gain the [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10) action. You can use Hunt Prey to designate only a creature that you've seen, heard about, or learned about through some other means, such as a bounty board or wanted poster. In addition to the other benefits of Hunt Prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) regarding your prey.

 If you already have Hunt Prey, you become an expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) and gain the circumstance bonus to Gather Information about your prey; you can still designate a creature you're tracking during exploration, in addition to the conditions above.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the bounty hunter archetype.

You Feast upon a [humanoid's](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) brain. The humanoid can't be [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) (or, if you're Feasting on a corpse, can't have been mindless while alive).

You consume the brains of your foe, causing synapses long rotten to fire and enabling you to shake off your mental torpor. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Branched Tree Of Pain](/Feats.aspx?ID=7188) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 41

**Usage**
imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage

</column>

---

The blade of your ikon takes one or more notches, capable of dealing mortal pain to your foes.

**Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.

**Transcendence**—Plant Thirty Barbs <actions string="Single Action" /> ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [transcendence](/Traits.aspx?ID=842)) You snap off a fragment of your ikon within your opponent’s body, which threatens to burst into numerous barbs. Make a Strike with your ikon. If successful, barbs fill the target, dealing two die of weapon damage the first time the creature uses a move action on each of its turns; the barbs are made out of the same material as your weapon ikon and bypass resistances and such accordingly (for instance, a cold iron spear would create cold iron barbs). The barbs last for 1d4 rounds. If the target dies while the barbs are still in their body, the barbs burst forth in a forest of thorns covering the creature’s space, which are greater difficult terrain and deal piercing damage equal to half your level for each square that is moved into.

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

---

The flames of your magic mark a target as an enemy of order. If your next action is to Cast a non-cantrip Spell that deals fire damage, that spell brands the target with a mark only you can see if it fails its saving throw. This brand lasts for 1 week. For as long as the target is branded, you always know the general direction and approximate distance of the target's current location, as long as it's on the same plane. You also know the direction the branded target is currently moving, if any, as well as any conditions affecting it. You can have only one brand active at a time.

>
[Brandish Authority](/Feats.aspx?ID=7327) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 112

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

With a terrifying pronouncement, you manifest a visible sign of your authority and fiendish power, such as a crown of flame upon your brow, a scepter forged of solidified souls, or a throne comprised of a dozen dragon skulls. This object appears in your space or in your hand, as appropriate, and remains for 1 minute. When your sign of power appears, attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) each enemy within 30 feet who can see or hear you. These Demoralize attempts don’t take any penalty for not sharing a language. As long as your sign of power remains manifested, your enemies can’t reduce the value of their [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition below 1.

You can spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) as part of performing this action; if you do, frightened creatures grovel before you, in awe of your terrible power. At the beginning of their turn, a creature that has the frightened condition from Brandish Authority must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. On failure, they must Drop Prone. On a critical failure, they must [Drop Prone](/Actions.aspx?ID=2295) and can’t Stand this turn.

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 72

**Archetype** [Snarecrafter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=265)

**Prerequisites**
[Snarecrafter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6414); [Snare Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=6506)

</column>

---

You've trained with the Brastlewark gnomes or studied their teachings, and learned the art of crafting their more magical snares. More information on magical snares can be found [here](Equipment.aspx?Category=31&Subcategory=120). You learn the formulas for crafting the _[pit illusion snare](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4343)_ and the _[shadow cloak snare](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4345)_ or two uncommon magical snares of your level or lower that you have access to. When you set a magical snare, the DC of any saving throw it requires uses your spell DC if that's higher. When you craft a non-magical snare, you can choose to give it the [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) trait. When you do so and the snare is one that normally deals damage, it deals an additional amount of force damage equal to its level.

<title level="2">Brastlewark Snare Engineering leads to...</title>
[Domino Effect](/Feats.aspx?ID=8905), [Remote Detonation](/Feats.aspx?ID=8903)

You can find the one weak point in a creature's scales, wards, or armor to get past its resistances. When you succeed at Exploit Vulnerability, you learn about the highest of the creature's resistances that can be bypassed (for example, if the creature has resistance to physical damage except silver), if the creature has one. If you prefer, you can choose the following benefit instead of one of the usual two benefits from Exploit Vulnerability.

 **Breached Defenses** You can choose this benefit only if you succeeded at Exploit Vulnerability and learned the creature has at least one resistance that can be bypassed. Choose one such resistance. Your unarmed and weapon Strikes bypass the chosen resistance.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Break the Causal Chain](/Feats.aspx?ID=7372) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Frequency**
once per month

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

Something terrible has happened. A beloved ally has fallen, a last stand has failed, or a tyrant has beaten you to a crucial goal. Whatever it is, your heart sinks. How can this be? No, this can’t be. You spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to alter reality as if you got a success (but not a critical success) with the [wish](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual. You must choose to completely undo the effects of a past action or set of actions that occurred within the past week to lead to the undesirable outcome. This will bring serious consequences back to haunt you some day. Altering the rhythm of causality is likely to draw the attention of certain [aeons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=357). [Fey norns](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3108) won’t be too happy with you fraying their precious threads of fate either. Deities whose domains include [change](/Domains.aspx?ID=40), [fate](/Domains.aspx?ID=75), [freedom](/Domains.aspx?ID=77), [time](/Domains.aspx?ID=54), or [tyranny](/Domains.aspx?ID=96) are likely to start keeping tabs on you, if they haven’t already, and send their agents to meddle in your affairs.

<summary>
Something terrible has happened.

fields.summary: Something terrible has happened.
fields.summary_markdown: Something terrible has happened.
fields.text: Feat 20 Break the Causal Chain Three Actions Concentrate Mythic Source War of Immortals pg. 125 Archetype Broken Chain Frequency once per month Prerequisites Broken Chain Dedication Something terrible has happened. A beloved ally has fallen, a last stand has failed, or a tyrant has beaten you to a crucial goal. Whatever it is, your heart sinks. How can this be? No, this can’t be. You spend a Mythic Point to alter reality as if you got a success (but not a critical success) with the wish ritual. You must choose to completely undo the effects of a past action or set of actions that occurred within the past week to lead to the undesirable outcome. This will bring serious consequences back to haunt you some day. Altering the rhythm of causality is likely to draw the attention of certain aeons. Fey norns won’t be too happy with you fraying their precious threads of fate either. Deities whose domains include change, fate, freedom, time, or tyranny are likely to start keeping tabs on you, if they haven’t already, and send their agents to meddle in your affairs.

Reddish ash stains your ikon, impossible to clean off. Every time you exhale, a tinge of red and a scent of spiced smoke float upon your breath. The imbued ikon gains the following ability.

Transcendence—Mark the Center <actions string="Single Action" /> (transcendence) You hold a hand to your lips and exhale, releasing enchanted red ash in a 15-foot cone. </title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #172: Secrets of the Temple City](/Sources.aspx?ID=102) pg. 79, [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 101

**Archetype** [Bright Lion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=129)

**Prerequisites**
member of the Bright Lions; not a worshipper of [Walkena](/Deities.aspx?ID=159); Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

**Access**
Bright Lion background

</column>

---

You become trained in your choice of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and in [Mzali Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. You incorporate enough worship of Walkena in your daily life to avoid suspicion. You typically don't need to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) or [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) to pass yourself off as a worshipper of [Walkena](/Deities.aspx?ID=159). Against careful inspection, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Deception checks specifically to pass yourself off as a version of yourself faithful to Walkena.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Bright Lion archetype.

<title level="2">Bright Lion Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blessing of the Sun Gods](/Feats.aspx?ID=3410), [Elude the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=2176), [Lion's Might](/Feats.aspx?ID=3411), [Sun's Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=2174), [Warding Light](/Feats.aspx?ID=2173)

---

The fire inside you asserts itself as beaming, radiant light. Your body is naturally luminescent, glowing with the effects of a primal [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171) cantrip. A cantrip is heightened to a spell level equal to half your level rounded up. The light is involuntary and constant; if [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371), it returns in 1d4 rounds. You suffer a –2 circumstance penalty on [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) and gain a +1 circumstance bonus on saves against [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) effects and effects that inflict the [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) or [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) conditions.

Your mother was a [sea hag](/Monsters.aspx?ID=254), granting you one sea-green or blue eye. You find comfort both in the sea and on the shore. Your elemental ancestor's legacy asserts itself as brackish water, like the seawater of the ocean. You gain the Salt Wound reaction.

**Salt Wound** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([undine](/Traits.aspx?ID=314)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature that has blood and is not at its maximum Hit Points hits you with a melee Strike; **Effect** You channel salt and brine from your blood into the creature's wounds. The creature must attempt a Fortitude save using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, the creature takes 1d6 [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) by the pain. On a critical failure, it instead takes 2d6 persistent acid damage and is sickened 2.

Success The target is unaffected. Failure The target’s attitude toward you improves by one step. Critical Failure The target’s attitude toward you improves by two steps.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

</column>

---

Your Calling was sparked by your outrage at tyrants, after having witnessed a brutal act of oppression that you could no longer abide. You may spend a Mythic Point when you attempt an [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) check to do so at mythic proficiency. Additionally, you gain the Ultimatum of Liberation action (see below), but you also gain the anathema, “You must not use Ultimatum of Liberation on a creature you don’t believe to be oppressing others or who has conceded their power”. If you break this anathema, you lose access to abilities granted by this archetype until you atone or make amends. 

Your GM has final say about what constitutes oppression, which can be a difficult and sometimes nebulous concept. In general, oppression is the cruel and unjust use of authority or power. Some examples include performing acts of violence against those without power, removing an individual’s agency through mind control magic, and engaging in organized mistreatment or exploitation of others. When the members of a royal guard assault a beggar just to get him off the street, that is oppression. When a tax collector levies higher charges against the less fortunate because it’s the law, they are participating in a system of oppression.

**Ultimatum of Liberation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You proclaim an ultimatum against a creature you believe is oppressing others and all who follow their orders. All other creatures (including you) who hear your ultimatum, or learn about it later on, are emboldened by your words for 1 day, and gain a +2 status bonus to their Will saving throws against effects produced by the oppressing creature and their allies, which increases to +3 if they are within 30 feet of you. Additionally, the first time each day that creature and each of its allies comes within 30 feet of you, they must succeed on a Will save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) or become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) (frightened 2 on a critical failure). This second effect has the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1524), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) traits. The oppressing creature may end all the effects as a free action by truthfully agreeing to permanently end their oppression. Otherwise, your Ultimatum of Liberation has no duration, though you can have only one Ultimatum of Liberation active at a time. If you pronounce a second Ultimatum of Liberation, the effects of the first one end.

<title level="2">Broken Chain Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bloc Tactics](/Feats.aspx?ID=7358), [Break the Causal Chain](/Feats.aspx?ID=7372), [Break the Cycle](/Feats.aspx?ID=7359), [Bring into the Fold](/Feats.aspx?ID=7364), [Cry of Rebellion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7365), [Liberty or Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=7369), [Lose Your Chains](/Feats.aspx?ID=7366), [Rebellious Existence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7370), [Release Me!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7360), [Remember thy Names](/Feats.aspx?ID=7367), [Reprisal of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7371), [Rites of Liberation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7361), [Stand Firm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7368), [United Front](/Feats.aspx?ID=7362), [You Can't Keep Us Down](/Feats.aspx?ID=7363), [You Can't Kill an Idea](/Feats.aspx?ID=7373)

<traits>

Your final blow can make an impact even if it rebounds off a foe’s defenses. Make a Strike with the required weapon. After the Strike, your turn ends. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Brutish Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=365) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 145

**Requirements**
You are wielding a two-handed melee weapon.

</column>

---

Throwing your weight behind your attack, you hit your opponent hard enough to make it stumble back. Make a Strike with a two-handed melee weapon. If you hit a target that is your size or smaller, that creature is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the end of your current turn, and you can automatically [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) it, with the same benefits as the Shove action (including the critical success effect, if your Strike was a critical hit). If you move to follow the target, your movement doesn't trigger reactions.

 This Strike has the following failure effect. 

**Failure** The target becomes flat-footed until the end of your current turn.

<title level="2">Brutish Shove leads to...</title>
[Flinging Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=408), [Powerful Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=373)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Jotunborn" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=860" />

</traits>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 14

once per day

</column>

---

The powers of creation that run through you allow you to conjure a temporary wall. You create a wall of dirt with the effects of [_wall of stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1751) with the following exceptions. The wall can be up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high and must stand vertically, preventing you from building other structures with it. Each 10-foot-by- 10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 20 Hit Points. The wall remains for 1 hour or until [Dismissed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Modification" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=410" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 24

</column>

---

You've built tools into your innovation so you can access and use them easily. When you take this feat, choose up to two sets of tools you own, such as [thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58) or [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25), that weigh a total of 2 Bulk or less. These tools become part of your innovation. The innovation's Bulk doesn't increase from this addition. As long as you are wielding, wearing, or adjacent to your innovation, you have the same quick access to these tools as the tools you are wearing, and they don't count against the usual limit of tools you can wear.

fields.text: Feat 1 Built-In Tools Inventor Modification Source Guns & Gears pg. 25 You’ve built tools into your innovation so you can access and use them easily. When you take this feat, choose up to two sets of tools you own, such as thieves’ tools or healer’s tools, that weigh a total of 2 Bulk or less. These tools become part of your innovation. The innovation’s Bulk doesn’t increase from this addition. As long as you are wielding, wearing, or adjacent to your innovation, you have the same quick access to these tools as the tools you are wearing, and they don’t count against the usual limit of tools you can wear.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bullet Dancer Burn](/Feats.aspx?ID=3236) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=117)

**Prerequisites**
[Bullet Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3235)

**Requirements**
You're wielding a firearm with an attached bayonet or reinforced stock.

</column>

---

The fiery blaze of your weapons combined with your unorthodox technique leaves your opponents with little opportunity to capitalize on any gaps in your defenses, or properly defend themselves against your onslaught. While in [Bullet Dancer Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3235), when you successfully Strike an opponent with a [bayonet](/Weapons.aspx?ID=186) or [reinforced stock](/Weapons.aspx?ID=187) attached to your firearm, the next ranged Strike you make against that opponent doesn't trigger reactions that would trigger on a ranged attack, such as [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256). While in Bullet Dancer Stance, when you make a successful ranged Strike against an opponent within your melee reach using a firearm, the next reinforced stock or bayonet attack attached to that firearm deals an additional 1 fire damage and 1 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) per weapon damage die.

 The benefit on your next Strike from either use of Bullet Dancer Burn is lost if not used by the end of your next turn.

<title level="2">Bullet Dancer Burn leads to...</title>
[Bullet Dancer Reload](/Feats.aspx?ID=3238)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bullet Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3235) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 132

**Archetype** [Bullet Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=117)

**Prerequisites**
expert in unarmored defense and trained in unarmed attack

</column>

---

You mix guns and melee into a deadly art. You gain the Bullet Dancer Stance action. You are also granted familiarity with [bayonets](/Weapons.aspx?ID=186), [reinforced stocks](/Weapons.aspx?ID=187), martial firearms, and martial [combination](/Traits.aspx?ID=417) weapons; for the purposes of proficiency and abilities from this archetype, you treat bayonets, reinforced stocks, martial firearms, and martial combination weapons as simple weapons. You gain access to uncommon combination weapons that have a firearm ranged form.

 **Bullet Dancer Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=152)) **Requirements** You're unarmored and wielding a simple [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16) or simple combination weapon; **Effect** You enter a specialized stance for a unique martial art centered around the use of simple firearms. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are those using bayonets, reinforced stocks, and simple firearms. You can use [Flurry of Blows](/Actions.aspx?ID=9) with these weapons. You can use your other [monk feats](/Feats.aspx?Traits=112) or [monk abilities](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) that normally require [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks with bayonets and reinforced stocks, so long as the feat or ability doesn't require a single, specific Strike. You can also use them with simple firearms when attacking within half the first range increment.

<title level="2">Bullet Dancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bullet Dancer Burn](/Feats.aspx?ID=3236), [Ranged Disarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3239)

---

You’ve learned how to synchronize traditional martial arts and guns. You gain the Bullet Dancer Stance action and are trained in bayonets and reinforced stocks. Whenever your proficiency in any weapon increases to expert or beyond, you gain that new proficiency with bayonets, reinforced stocks, simple firearms and unarmed attacks.

**Bullet Dancer Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=701)) **Requirements** You’re unarmored and wielding a simple firearm, bayonet, or reinforced stock; **Effect** You enter a specialized stance for a unique martial art centered around the use of simple firearms. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are those using bayonets, reinforced stocks, and simple firearms. You can use [Flurry of Blows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2817) with these weapons. You can use your other monk feats or monk abilities that normally require unarmed attacks with [bayonets](/Weapons.aspx?ID=186) and [reinforced stocks](/Weapons.aspx?ID=187), so long as the feat or ability doesn’t require a single, specific Strike. You can also use them with simple firearms when attacking within half the first range increment.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the bullet dancer dedication archetype.

[Bullet Dancer Burn](/Feats.aspx?ID=8741), [Ranged Disarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=8744)

</column>

---

You transport yourself up to 1 mile, as a 5th-rank [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) spell. Everyone who has seen you in the last 24 hours must succeed at a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or forget your physical appearance as though affected by a 6th-rank [_rewrite memory_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1655) spell. You can choose to exempt any number of creatures from this effect. You can instead Burn Identity as an activity that takes 10 minutes. If you do, instead of the effects of translocate, you can instantly teleport yourself and up to four targets touched (either willing creatures or objects roughly the size of a creature) to the nearest border of Andoran, in addition to its other effects.

The target then attempts a Fortitude save against your class DC. **Critical Success** The sigil immediately vanishes, and the creature is unaffected.
**Success** The sigil acts as a magnet for your fiery attacks, granting the creature a –1 penalty to its saves and AC against your fire impulses. The sigil lasts until the end of your next turn or until the creature spends at least 1 action obeying your command, whichever happens first.
**Failure** At the start of the creature’s next turn, if it doesn’t use their first action to obey the command, the sigil ignites as it vanishes, dealing 8d6 fire damage and 2d6 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to the creature.
**Critical Failure** The creature must spend the first action of its next turn to obey your command; it can’t [Delay](/Actions.aspx?ID=2294). The sigil vanishes at the end of its turn; it ignites if the creature didn’t use all its remaining actions to continue to obey your command, dealing 8d6 fire damage and 2d6 persistent fire damage to the creature. --- **Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6, and the persistent damage increases by 1d6.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Burning Surge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7423) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Wildspell](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=295)

**Prerequisites**
[Wildspell Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7418)

**Trigger**
A creature [Casts a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144) within your [_spellsurge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2150) aura.

</column>

---

You cause a surge of magical energy to flare up, harming that creature and those near it. The triggering creature and all creatures adjacent to it take 1d6 damage per rank of the spell ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher). The damage is of the same type as dealt by the spell (or one type of damage of your choosing if the spell deals multiple types of damage). If the spell doesn’t deal damage, the damage is mental. The effect gains the trait of the damage dealt. If you spend a Mythic Point as part of using this reaction, calculate the DC with mythic proficiency; you can also choose to deal [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), or [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) damage instead of the type that would normally be dealt, and creatures that fail the saving throw take [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) of the same type as the base effect equal to the rank of the triggering creature’s spell.

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 73 **Archetype** [Swarmkeeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=223) **Prerequisites** [Swarmkeeper Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5463) --- Your swarm takes on characteristics of the death cicadas of the Mana Wastes, whose distinctive buzz is said to be a herald of imminent demise. The inclusion of these death cicadas grants your swarm a fly Speed of 20 feet. You also gain the Death Drone action. **Death Drone** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [flourish](/Traits.aspx?ID=606), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) The cicadas in your swarm make a droning sound that stimulates a fear response. Each creature within your swarm's space takes 6d4 mental damage and must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creatures takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage, is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76), and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks that require hearing.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, is frightened 2, and is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) until the start of your next turn.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 52 **Frequency** once per hour **Requirements** You must know the target’s name. --- In a moment of inspiration, you understand the target perfectly, allowing you to craft a rune that draws effects to the target by their very name. Attempt a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check against a [standard DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2629) of the target creature’s level. Regardless of the outcome, you can’t attempt to use By Your Name against the target again for 24 hours. **Critical Success** You understand the target’s runic name and temporarily learn how to write their name as a special diacritic rune. This diacritic rune magnifies the effects of the base rune when targeting the named creature. When the rune is invoked, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their saving throw against the effects of the base rune, and if the base rune deals damage, it gains a status bonus to its damage equal to half your level. The inspiration used to understand this diacritic rune fades quickly, and you forget how to use the diacritic rune after 1 minute.
**Success** As critical success, but the rune doesn’t grant a bonus to damage.

Critical Success You understand the target’s runic name and temporarily learn how to write their name as a special diacritic rune. This diacritic rune magnifies the effects of the base rune when targeting the named creature. When the rune is invoked, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their saving throw against the effects of the base rune, and if the base rune deals damage, it gains a status bonus to its damage equal to half your level. The inspiration used to understand this diacritic rune fades quickly, and you forget how to use the diacritic rune after 1 minute. Success As critical success, but the rune doesn’t grant a bonus to damage.

You build a powerful magical connection with a chosen gun or crossbow, gaining the ability to conjure it directly to your hand from any distant location. During your daily preparations, choose a single crossbow or firearm. Until your next daily preparations, you can use the Call Gun action to call the gun to your hand.

 **Call Gun** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) **Effect** You hold aloft a free hand and call the firearm or crossbow you chose during your daily preparations into your hand. As long as the weapon you chose is on the same plane, it appears in your hand.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 42

**Requirements**
You have a free hand.

</column>

---

You can tug on the bonds of ownership between yourself and your [implement](/Implements.aspx), causing it to find its way back to you. You look down and find that your implement has mysteriously appeared in your free hand, as long as the implement was within 1 mile and on the same plane of existence. If your implement is attended by another creature, that creature can prevent the implement from teleporting away if it succeeds at a Will save against your class DC. If the creature succeeds, you can't attempt to Call that Implement again; you must track the creature down to get the implement back.

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 13

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You can call upon the ancient powers bestowed on you by the gods to create any tools you might need at a moment’s notice. You conjure forth a simple tool, such as a shovel or hammer, into your hands. This tool remains conjured until your next daily preparations so long as it’s on your person. If the tool leaves your possession for more than 1 minute, it falls apart into a pile of silk that then dissolves into nothingness. 

At 9th level, you can use this ability once per hour instead of once per day. When using it in this way, you can maintain only one tool at a time; any previous tool you conjured dissolves into nothingness.

    pfs="Standard"

[Call the Hurricane](/Feats.aspx?ID=4274) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

Massive waves spiral around you, with you as the eye of the hurricane. The waves appear in a 20-foot emanation, or a 30-foot emanation if you're in a body of water. Each creature in the area takes 6d8 bludgeoning damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that fails its save is battered by the waves and [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or 20 feet on a critical failure).

---
**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d8.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ratfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=769" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 31

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Ratspeak](/Feats.aspx?ID=5655)

</column>

---

You give a shrill whistle and point, and a massive swarm of rats pours forth from the surrounding terrain to fill a 30-foot burst within 120 feet. The rats scurry over the ground and climb up walls and surfaces, biting and clawing as they deal 6d8 piercing damage to all enemies in the area. The rats continue to swarm in the area for the next minute, dealing 3d8 piercing damage to any enemy that ends its turn in the area and transforming the area into [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) (though the rats allow you and your allies to pass normally). You can Dismiss the effect.

You have heard the Call, and in constantly resisting that persistent demand, you've developed a mental bulwark against effects that would target your mind. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects. If you roll a success on your saving throw against a mental effect that would make you [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6), you get a critical success instead.

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 115 --- You target a specific area of your foe's anatomy to debilitating effect. Declare a part of your foe's anatomy to target and make a ranged weapon Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target takes one of the following effects, based on the body part you targeted. The GM should use the stated effects as a guideline when attacking creatures with stranger anatomy—for instance, applying the “arms” effect to a creature's tentacles if those are what the creature uses to attack.
  • **Arms** The target is [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, it's also enfeebled 1 for 1 minute.
  • **Head** The target is [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, it's also stupefied 1 for 1 minute.
  • **Legs** The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, it also takes a –5-foot penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute.
  • **Wings** If the target is flying using its wings, it immediately falls 20 feet, or 40 feet on a critical hit. The fall is gradual enough that if the target hits the ground, it takes no damage from the fall.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Changeling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=212" />
<trait label="Lineage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=317" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 31

</column>

---

You are among the most common of changelings—those born to [green hags](/Monsters.aspx?ID=255)—and a vibrant green eye signifies that parentage. Your mother's manipulative nature and versatile voice gives you an edge when deceiving others. You gain the [Charming Liar](/Feats.aspx?ID=766) skill feat. If you roll [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) for initiative, foes in that combat encounter that haven't acted yet are [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against you.

</title>

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Campfire Chronicler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=300)

You’ve gained Isthralei’s attention and can now offer stories up to him, either passing on your own stories or collecting those of travelers as he did. You become trained in Religion and Survival; for either of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the Offer Story action.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Hobgoblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=268" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 35

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
An adjacent and willing ally would be reduced to 0 HP but not killed.

</column>

---

You physically help an ally remain standing and encourage them to push through their pain against dire odds. Your ally doesn't fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and remains at 1 Hit Point. The ally also gains a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute. Fighting onward with such an injury isn't without consequence; your ally's [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) condition increases by 1.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Can't You See?](/Feats.aspx?ID=3763) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 64

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); Expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

The eye rebels, the mind recoils—no matter how much those who can see you try to explain what's there, their friends' gazes just skitter over you, like a bird afraid to land. A character who attempts to [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=97) your location must attempt a DC 14 flat check. If they fail, their allies misunderstand them and aren't sure where you are. On a critical failure, their allies think they pointed you out in a different location entirely, chosen by the GM. Similarly, when a creature critically fails to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) you while you're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by it, it thinks you're in a different location chosen by the GM. In either case, you appear to be hidden to a creature that thinks you're in a different location, though you're actually undetected by it for targeting and further uses of the Seek action.

>
[Cannibalize Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=4049) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Universal Ancestry" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=467" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 127

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Fey Influence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1239)

</column>

---

The fey magic inside of you is a vital part of your body, and you can steal other sources of magic to replenish yours. You can draw power from your magical equipment to replenish your health. You drain one of your [invested](/Traits.aspx?ID=98) items, in the process regaining Hit Points equal to double the item's level.

 In addition, you can attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with a total bonus equal to 10 + the drained item's level against one effect that gave you the [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15), or [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) condition. If you succeed, you reduce the chosen condition's value by 1.

 An item drained by this action becomes non-magical until the next time you make your daily preparations.

**Special** This feat gains the trait appropriate for your ancestry ([human](/Traits.aspx?ID=90) for [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=81) for [goblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=4), etc.).

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

---

By loading special ammunition in a particular way, you can make your [siege weapons](/SiegeWeapons.aspx) do all manner of tricks that other siege engineers can barely even imagine. If you personally contribute an additional [Load](/Rules.aspx?ID=1624) action to the siege weapon's loading, above the minimum, you can change a burst into a line twice as long as the size of the burst, or vice versa (so a 10-foot burst turns into a 20-foot line, or a 20-foot line turns into a 10-foot burst).

fields.access: You're from the Shackles
fields.markdown:
**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 93 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) **Access** You're from the Shackles **Requirements** You are above an enemy. --- You’ve learned how to make a quick descent with a sudden stop—directly on an enemy. You intentionally fall onto an enemy within 10 feet of you horizontally and can accurately target them from up to a height equal to 5 feet times your level. You take damage as [normal](/Rules.aspx?ID=2352); the enemy must attempt a Reflex save against your class DC with the following results, instead of the usual rules for [falling on a creature](/Rules.aspx?ID=2353). If an ability reduces the amount of damage you take from falling, the enemy’s damage is based on the damage you would have taken before that reduction. In addition, if you have a means of controlling your descent, such as holding onto a rope or sliding down an adjacent wall, you do not land [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) even if you take damage from the fall. **Critical Success** The enemy takes no damage.
**Success** The enemy takes bludgeoning damage equal to one quarter the falling damage you took.
**Failure** The creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to half the falling damage you took and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage you took from the fall, is knocked prone, and is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1.

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Verduran Shadow](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=312)

**Prerequisites**
[Verduran Shadow Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7606); Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)

</column>

---

You are as at home in the treetops as you are beneath their branches. You gain a [climb Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349) of 15 feet when moving through trees, vines, and other foliage. Whenever you succeed at an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) a tree or an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) on a branch, you get a critical success instead. You aren’t [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while Climbing or Balancing on a tree.

Charisma +2; you don't have an [animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2113), [construct companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=1600), or other companion that functions similarly

</column>

---

You become trained in your choice of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40); if you are already trained in both of these skills, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You also gain your choice of the [Group Impression](/Feats.aspx?ID=5155) or the [Group Coercion](/Feats.aspx?ID=5154) skill feat. If you already have both of these skill feats, you gain another 1st level skill feat for which you qualify.  

You also gain the assistance of a dedicated follower, who has agreed to accompany you on your journeys. They have the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait and begin as a novice follower. [See followers](/Followers.aspx) for more information.

**Special** Once you have a follower, you can never take a feat or class feature that grants an animal companion or another companion that prevents you from having an animal companion.

<title level="2">Captain Dedication leads to...</title>
[Additional Follower](/Feats.aspx?ID=7995), [Cadre](/Feats.aspx?ID=7998), [Coordinated Tactics](/Feats.aspx?ID=8001), [Experienced Follower](/Feats.aspx?ID=7996), [Leader of All](/Feats.aspx?ID=7997), [Legendary Leader](/Feats.aspx?ID=8003), [Peerless Captain](/Feats.aspx?ID=8004), [Tactical Guidance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7999)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Captivating Intensity](/Feats.aspx?ID=3360) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Captivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=125)

**Prerequisites**
[Basic Captivator Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=3359)

</column>

---

Your ability to captivate others has grown, and you can use your captivator abilities more often. You seem to never run out of the ability to fascinate or distract. You can cast each occult innate spell granted by captivator archetype feats one additional time per day. You can do this for spells of all levels granted, other than your two highest spell levels from non-cantrip captivator spells. If you have [Heightened Captivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3362), you can Cast the chosen Spell a second time each day, though one of the two times you cast it, it's heightened two levels lower than your highest level of non-cantrip captivator spells, as long as the spell can be cast at that spell level.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Captivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3358) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 120

**Archetype** [Captivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=125)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14; Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

Your ability to captivate others borders on the preternatural. You are seldom at a loss in social situations, and you can create minor [enchantments](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) or [illusions](/Traits.aspx?ID=92). Choose Deception or Diplomacy. You become trained in that skill, or become an expert if you were already trained.

 Choose two cantrips from the [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) list; each cantrip must be from either the enchantment or illusion school. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity and can cast these spells as occult innate spells. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs. If you have a hand free, you can usually replace material components with somatic components, so you don't need to use a spell [component pouch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=33). Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the captivator archetype.

<title level="2">Captivator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Captivator Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=3359), [Effortless Captivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3365), [Heightened Captivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3362), [Look Again](/Feats.aspx?ID=3367), [Reactive Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3364)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756)

**Trigger**
You succeed at your save against a foe's harmful spell, or a foe fails a spell attack roll against you from a harmful spell.

</column>

---

When you resist a spell, you capture some of its magic for your own use. You enter your Arcane Cascade stance, using the triggering spell to determine what damage type your Arcane Cascade deals. Alternatively, if you're already in Arcane Cascade, you can instead amplify its effects temporarily. Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +2 status bonus to the damage from your Arcane Cascade.

You’ve explored enough dusty tombs and hidden vaults to gain a sixth sense about traps, and you sometimes notice them even when you’re not trying to. Even if you aren’t Searching in exploration mode, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to Search for them. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

    right="Feat 1"

[Caretaker's Intuition](/Feats.aspx?ID=7769) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 13

</column>

---

Your forebears had a deep understanding of the natural world around them, and you’ve learned some of their knowledge and techniques. You are trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43). If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. 

Additionally, while outdoors, you can spend 10 minutes to read the sky and determine upcoming weather. You get a general impression of weather up to 8 hours in advance. You can use this to determine that clear skies or a rainstorm are ahead, but you can’t determine specifics like wind speeds and direction, or that a tornado would be occurring later.

---

When your swarm is sharing your space and Strides, you can choose to have your swarm carry you with it. You stay in the same basic position within its space while it moves and when you arrive at your new location (with your exact location determined by the GM if it's unclear). Because you're moving voluntarily, your movement isn't [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) and therefore still triggers reactions based on movement. If your swarm [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), and you don't have a fly Speed, you fall at the end of this movement.

>
[Cascading Ray](/Feats.aspx?ID=2868) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your last action was a successful Spellstrike, and the spell you cast dealt energy damage (acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, negative, positive, or sonic).

</column>

---

Magical energy spills out to extend beyond the creature you struck. The flowing energy forms a ray with a range of 60 feet from the creature you damaged. You can't target any of the creatures you damaged with your Spellstrike with the ray. Make a spell attack roll against the new target's AC, at the same multiple attack penalty as the Strike. On a hit, the target of the ray takes 1d4 damage per spell level of the same type of energy damage the spell deals (double damage on a critical hit). If you cast the spell in your Spellstrike from a spell slot, the damage from Cascading Ray increases to 1d8 damage per spell level.

 If the spell deals more than one type of energy damage, you choose only one for the ray. This ray has the [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15) trait, the school and tradition traits of the original spell, and the trait matching the damage type.

You attempt to cast a malevolent entity out of the creature or object it's possessing. Roll a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against the [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129) effect; you must be within 30 feet of the possessed creature or object to do so. Your counteract level is half your level rounded up, and your counteract modifier is your [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) modifier, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) modifier, or spell DC – 10, whichever is highest. If you succeed, the entity is driven out and can't attempt to possess that creature or object for 1 week. If you fail, the possessing creature is immune to your Cast Out for a year and a day.

---

Growing up among catfolk has taught you the traditional values of freedom to travel, stewardship of the land, and quick reactions when your curiosity lands you in trouble. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also become trained in [Catfolk Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8).

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Cathartic Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2963) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 194

**Archetype** [Cathartic Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=97)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14 or ability to cast spells from spell slots

</column>

---

You've learned to harness a particular emotion and mix it into your magic. Choose an emotion from the Emotional States section below to be your catharsis emotion.

 If you don't already cast spells from spell slots, you learn to cast spontaneous spells and gain the Cast a Spell activity. You gain a spell repertoire with one cantrip of your choice, from a spell list of your choice. You choose this cantrip from the common spells on your chosen spell list or from other spells to which you have access on that list. You're trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for that tradition. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

 If you can already cast spells from spell slots, you learn one additional cantrip from your spellcasting tradition. If you're a prepared caster, you can prepare this spell in addition to your usual cantrips per day; if you're a spontaneous caster, you add this cantrip to your spell repertoire.

 You gain the Catharsis reaction and the Settle Emotions activity.

 **Catharsis** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Trigger** determined by your catharsis emotion; **Effect** You gain the catharsis activation effects listed for your catharsis emotion. You gain that emotion's emotional fervor benefits for 3 rounds. When your emotional fervor ends, you suffer the listed emotional fallout. After using Catharsis, you can't use it again until you use the Settle Emotions activity.

 **Settle Emotions** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) You spend 10 minutes using techniques you've developed to calm your emotions and bring them back under control. This allows you to access your Catharsis again.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the cathartic mage archetype.

<title level="2">Cathartic Mage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Cathartic Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=2964), [Cathartic Focus Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2965), [Infectious Emotions](/Feats.aspx?ID=2968), [Work Yourself Up](/Feats.aspx?ID=2966)

Catharsis Reaction (concentrate, emotion, mental) Trigger determined by your catharsis emotion; Effect You gain the catharsis activation effects listed for your catharsis emotion. You gain that emotion's emotional fervor benefits for 3 rounds. When your emotional fervor ends, you suffer the listed emotional fallout. After using Catharsis, you can't use it again until you use the Settle Emotions activity. Settle Emotions (concentrate, emotion, mental) You spend 10 minutes using techniques you've developed to calm your emotions and bring them back under control. This allows you to access your Catharsis again. Special You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the cathartic mage archetype. Cathartic Mage Dedication leads to... Basic Cathartic Spellcasting, Cathartic Focus Spell, Infectious Emotions, Work Yourself Up

You can use the [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) activity to create [oils](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=17) and [potions](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=18). You immediately gain the formulas for four common 1st-level oils or potions. At 4th level and every 2 levels beyond that, you gain the formula for a common oil or potion of that level or lower (a 4th-level potion if you're 4th level, a 6th-level potion if you're 6th level, and so on). If you have a familiar, you can have your familiar learn these formulas rather than storing them in a formula book. Your familiar can learn new formulas in the same way it learns new spells, and these formulas are transferred from a slain familiar to a new familiar in the same way spells are.

 You can brew a great deal of magic within your cauldron. When you Craft a batch of oils or potions, you can make up to six in a batch instead of the usual four per batch.

</traits>

</column>

---

You can brew magic in your cauldron, creating useful magical concoctions. You can use the Craft activity to create oils and potions. You immediately gain the formulas for four common 1st-level oils or potions. At 4th level and every 2 levels beyond that, you gain the formula for a common oil or potion of that level or lower (a 4th-level potion if you’re 4th level, a 6th-level potion if you’re 6th level, and so on). If you have a familiar, you can have your familiar learn these formulas rather than storing them in a formula book. Your familiar can learn new formulas in the same way it learns new spells, and these formulas are transferred from a slain familiar to a new familiar in the same way spells are.

During your daily preparations, you can create one temporary oil or potion using a formula you know. If you have master proficiency in spell DC, you can create a batch of two temporary oils or potions during your daily preparations, and if you have legendary proficiency, you can create a batch of three. Any items you create this way become inert bottles of liquid the next time you make your daily preparations, and any remaining effects of the temporary items end. A temporary oil or potion has no value.

You have specialized glands inside your throat, which produce acidic nectar that you can spit long distances. You gain a nectar ranged [unarmed attack](/Rules.aspx?ID=1584) with a range increment of 20 feet that deals 1d4 acid damage. On a critical hit, the target is additionally [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1. Your nectar doesn’t add [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effects. You’re [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to your own nectar.

**Special** This feat gains the trait for your ancestry.

---

You gain a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=151) that serves as your mount. You can choose from [animal companions](/Companions.aspx) with the mount special ability, as well as any additional options from your pledge, as determined by your GM. You must choose an animal companion that's at least one size larger than you, but if the animal usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the cavalier archetype. This restriction is waived if you have pledged to the organization associated with the other dedication feat. For example, if you are pledged to a Hellknight order, you could take Hellknight dedication feats without needing to gain other feats from the cavalier archetype first.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 192

**Archetype** [Cavalier](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=244)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)

</column>

---

You gain a young animal companion that serves as your mount. You can choose from animal companions with the mount special ability, as well as any additional options from your pledge (see Cavalier Pledges sidebar), as determined by your GM. You must choose an animal companion that’s at least one size larger than you, but if the animal usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).

**Special** If you have pledged yourself to a cause, you can take a second dedication feat closely tied to that cause even if you haven’t taken two additional cavalier feats. For instance, if you pledged yourself to fight crime with a group of vigilantes, you could take the vigilante dedication without first completing the cavalier archetype. The GM determines what archetypes, if any, are valid choices.

<title level="2">Cavalier Dedication leads to...</title>
[Abrasive Drag](/Feats.aspx?ID=9517), [Born In The Saddle](/Feats.aspx?ID=9514), [Cavalier's Banner](/Feats.aspx?ID=6287), [Cavalier's Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6288), [Cushion Landing](/Feats.aspx?ID=7986), [Dashing Pickup](/Feats.aspx?ID=7988), [Defend Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=6291), [Impressive Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=6289), [Legendary Rider](/Feats.aspx?ID=6297), [Mounted Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=6292), [Mounting Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=7987), [Quick Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=6290), [Rearing Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=7990), [Reckless Riding Lunge](/Feats.aspx?ID=9515), [Ride-by Recovery](/Feats.aspx?ID=9516), [Trampling Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6294), [Unseat](/Feats.aspx?ID=6295), [Vaulting Gallop](/Feats.aspx?ID=7989)

<title level="3">Cavalier Pledges</title> Many cavaliers pledge themselves in service to a specific organization or individual, such as a noble family or sovereign ruler, a knightly order or another organization, or particular ideal. A cavalier pledged to an order or ideal must uphold its edicts and is beholden to any anathema it has; for example, a cavalier pledged to the druid's animal order would be tied to that anathema, while a cavalier pledged to the church of Abadar would be held to the same standards as a cleric of that god. If you pledge yourself to an entity or cause without a stated anathema, you should work with your GM to determine the edicts and anathema associated with your pledge. Cavaliers who have pledged themselves can gain access to certain abilities related to that pledge, such as Cavalier's Banner. If you violate the anathema of your pledge, you lose access to those feats until you benefit from an [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual. Changing the subject of your pledge is equivalent to retraining a class feature.
