You are a cel rau, child of a strigoi, one of the first vampires to walk Golarion. Your heritage ties you to the [Shadow Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=11) and grants you strange resilience to light and darkness alike. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects with the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), or [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) traits, and whenever you become [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) or [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for at least 2 rounds, you can reduce the duration by 1 round.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

</column>

---

You imbue a fragment of your divine spark into a weapon, blessing your blade and transforming it into a weapon worthy of the celestial realms. Select one weapon or [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086) when you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575). The weapon sheds light like a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2760), deals an additional 1d8 spirit damage, and creatures who wield it gain the weapon’s [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203).

When you critically hit a target with the weapon, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) or be [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1d4 rounds. 

As a single action that has the [concentration](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait, you can hold your hand aloft and call this weapon back to your possession; it immediately teleports into your hand.

While you’re holding this weapon, you can spend 1 Mythic Point as a single action to temporarily grant a blessing to weapons wielded by your allies. Each ally within the [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) of your nimbus when you take this action selects one weapon in their possession. For 1 minute, the selected weapons gain the following benefits: the weapon sheds light like a torch, the weapon deals an additional 1d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage, and creatures who wield the weapon gain the weapon’s critical specialization.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Celestial Cacophony](/Feats.aspx?ID=7080) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=604" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=697" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 111

**Prerequisites**
[weapon innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3)

**Access**
Tian Xia origin

</column>

---

Your weapon contains a detonation chamber that launches fireworks, sparklers, and black powder pellets that sizzle, twist, and scatter on the ground in a cacophonous manner liable to annoy the entire Celestial Court. All creatures in a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) extending from your innovation take 3d4 fire damage and 3d4 [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC; both the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) and sonic damage increase by 1d4 at 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter. The area affected by the cone becomes [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) until the start of your next turn. Creatures moving through this area must succeed at a Reflex save against your class DC or take 2d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).

**Unstable Function** You rattle your weapon violently to make it belch out even more pyrotechnics. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Celestial Cacophony. The area increases to a 30-foot cone, and all damage dice increase from d4s to d8s.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Celestial Rebirth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7344) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 117

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

</column>

---

Through your diligence and commitment to heroics, you finally complete your apotheosis into a true [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551). Your appearance changes as desired, becoming a perfect expression of your true self. You cease aging, and you can’t die from old age. You become immune to [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) and [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578). You gain the celestial and [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) traits, as well as the [agathion](/Traits.aspx?ID=349), [angel](/Traits.aspx?ID=530), [archon](/Traits.aspx?ID=536), or [azata](/Traits.aspx?ID=543) trait, depending on whose ranks you are joining. 

You become a vessel of vitality. You can cast [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1456) once per day as a 5th-rank innate [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell and [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) twice per day as a 7th-rank innate divine spell. When you [cast a spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) trait that doesn’t target you, you channel this healing energy through your own body before releasing it. You regain 1d6 Hit Points per level of the spell. In addition, you can cast [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1645) as a 10th-rank innate divine spell. When you do, the cost to cast this spell changes to “spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320).”

If you die, you’re immediately reborn as a [nephilim](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=68) of an ancestry of your choosing or decided in conjunction with your GM. You are descended from the celestials whose trait you bear—agathion, angel, archon, or azata. This might be represented by a lineage feat. You can choose if you will be reborn on [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), [Elysium](/Planes.aspx?ID=40), [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41), or [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=44). Regardless of where you’re reborn, celestials watch over you, keeping you safe throughout your life. When you reach the age of maturity, you regain your previous powers and memories, becoming an ascended celestial once again. These memories are faint and dreamlike, as if they happened to another person, giving you perspective and history, but not supplanting your current personality or emotional connections.

Your growing connection to your celestial forebears has granted you one of their resistances as well. Choose one of the following energy damage types: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. You gain resistance 5 to that damage type.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 113

**Archetype** [Lastwall Sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15)

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Warden](/Feats.aspx?ID=887)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12).

</column>

---

You take on a stance that marks your location as a place where none will fall. When you enter this stance and at the beginning of each of your turns while in Cenotaph Stance, you gain 10 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last until the start of your next turn. If you move or are forced to move, you automatically leave Cenotaph Stance. While in Cenotaph Stance, you’re treated as always having the required shield raised. In addition, you can use your [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction when an ally within 15 feet of you takes physical damage, in addition to its normal trigger, thus preventing the ally from taking damage instead of you. Finally, you gain an additional reaction at the start of each of your turns that can be used only for Shield Block.

**Special** If you can use Shield Block to reduce damage that isn’t physical damage (for instance, if you have the [Bless Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=3598) or [Necromantic Bulwark](/Feats.aspx?ID=3606) feat), you can use your Shield Block reaction when an ally within 15 feet of you takes damage that you could prevent with Shield Block.

fields.text: Feat 20 Cenotaph Stance Single Action Archetype Stance Source Claws of the Tyrant pg. 113 Archetype Lastwall Sentry Prerequisites Lastwall Warden Requirements You’re wielding a shield. You take on a stance that marks your location as a place where none will fall. When you enter this stance and at the beginning of each of your turns while in Cenotaph Stance, you gain 10 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of your next turn. If you move or are forced to move, you automatically leave Cenotaph Stance. While in Cenotaph Stance, you’re treated as always having the required shield raised. In addition, you can use your Shield Block reaction when an ally within 15 feet of you takes physical damage, in addition to its normal trigger, thus preventing the ally from taking damage instead of you. Finally, you gain an additional reaction at the start of each of your turns that can be used only for Shield Block. Special If you can use Shield Block to reduce damage that isn’t physical damage (for instance, if you have the Bless Shield or Necromantic Bulwark feat), you can use your Shield Block reaction when an ally within 15 feet of you takes damage that you could prevent with Shield Block.

You have prepared a special knife to direct energies when spellcasting. During your daily preparations, you and your familiar can perform a short ritual over a weapon in the knife group—typically a dagger. This causes the knife to function as a magic wand, containing any one 1st-rank spell your familiar knows. You, and only you, can Activate the knife to Cast the Spell within it, as normal for a [wand](/Rules.aspx?ID=756). You can attempt to overcharge the knife, and this can break or destroy the knife as normal. You can have only one ceremonial knife at a time.

At 8th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the maximum rank of spell your ceremonial knife can hold increases by 1.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chain Infusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=4197) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Infusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=503" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 23

</column>

---

The elemental matter in your blast keeps reconstituting itself to travel onward, no matter how many bodies it collides with. If your next action is an [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) and it hits, attempt a new ranged Elemental Blast from the target against a different creature that's within the blast's range, measuring from the creature you hit. You can keep chaining the blast in this way each time you hit. Your multiple attack penalty applies normally to any blasts in the chain after the first. You can make up to five blasts total, but you can't target the same creature more than once. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. (If you start with a melee blast, you still add your Strength to only that blast, not the successive ranged blasts.)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chain of Words](/Feats.aspx?ID=9197) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=75" />
<trait label="Invocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=956" />
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 51

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

</column>

---

You see the thin lines of magic between your creations, and you can exploit that connection with a small shift of power from one rune to another. You [Invoke two Runes](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) within 60 feet. In addition to the runes’ normal effects, a chain of glowing script flows between them, dealing 5d6 force damage to all creatures in a straight [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) between them with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex saving throw; creatures bearing the invoked runes are not in the area of this line. A creature who critically fails its save is also [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296), as the runes seal its movements. The DC to Escape is your class DC. 

At 12th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chain Reaction](/Feats.aspx?ID=3279) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 143

**Archetype** [Unexpected Sharpshooter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=123)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Unexpected Sharpshooter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3272)

</column>

---

You fire your gun once, creating a devastating and unpredictable chain of events; perhaps your bullet strikes exactly the right spot on a water tower, causing it to flood and incite a stampede of horses which knock over a lantern that sets a city on fire. Whatever the exact chain reaction, and no matter how improbable, the indiscriminate catastrophe creates significant challenges for your enemies across a wide area while leaving everyone else alone.

 Make a Strike with a ranged weapon, and if you hit, you can make another Strike at a target within 30 feet of the first target. If you hit the second target, attempt to Strike a third target within 30 feet of the second target, and so on, continuing until you miss a target. You can cease the chain at any point; otherwise, it ends when you first miss an attack. However, you can't target the same creature more than once; each time you move to a new target, it must be a target you haven't made a Strike against yet during this particular use of Chain Reaction.

 This damage is caused by some improbable set of events that injures one target after another, rather than from actually making several shots. Perhaps you shot at a tree branch that then fell on the targets, or one target's scream caused another to accidentally set off their gun and shoot themselves in the foot. This means that only the first target suffers any special effects tied to the bullet (if it was magical ammunition, for example), but each target you hit still takes the same damage dealt by your Strike. Normally, all damage is of the same damage type as the initial bullet. However, the GM might choose to change the damage type based on their description of the chain reaction. For example, if one target was burned by fire, that target might take fire damage instead of physical damage.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Challenge Insight](/Feats.aspx?ID=7562) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 289

**Archetype** [Palatine Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=306)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Palatine Detective Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7557)

**Trigger**
A creature you can see [Casts a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that is from the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) or [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) tradition.

**Requirements**
The triggering caster must be able to hear and understand you.

</column>

---

Your deep grasp of the mystical lets you know exactly what to say to make others doubt how well they understand the source of their own power. Attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) check against the triggering spell. Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up. You use your [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) modifier as your counteract modifier if the triggering spell is from the [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) tradition, or your [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) modifier if the triggering spell is from the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) tradition. If you successfully counteract the spell, the caster becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 until the end of their next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Champion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6196) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=659" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 177

**Archetype** [Champion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=230)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma +2; Strength +2

</column>

---

Choose a deity. You are bound by your deity’s anathema and gain the champion’s aura and sanctification as described in the [champion](/Classes.aspx?ID=58) class. Choose a cause as you would if you were a champion, with the same options a champion must abide by. You gain its edicts and anathema but don’t gain the other abilities.

You become trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in champion class DC. If you later gain a devotion spell, you become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. 

You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you’re 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

<title level="2">Champion Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Devotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=6197), [Champion Resiliency](/Feats.aspx?ID=6198), [Champion's Reaction](/Feats.aspx?ID=6201), [Devout Blessing](/Feats.aspx?ID=6202), [Devout Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=6199)

<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />

Your previous life ended due to sheer poor luck, struck by lightning or choking on a fish bone. You can reroll the triggering recovery check or saving throw, but you must use the new result, even if it's worse than the first roll.

**Special** You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187)

**Prerequisites**
[Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807)

</column>

---

You know that for the best disguise to work, one requires not only the right skills but also the right look—luckily you can copy both using special magical techniques. When you [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), you don't need a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19); instead, simple illusions or temporary transmutations ripple over your body like mirror shards, providing the supplies that the kit ordinarily would. When you Impersonate in this way, your Impersonate activity gains the [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait.

>
[Channel Divine Spark](/Feats.aspx?ID=7335) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

</column>

---

You embrace your divine spark, unleashing your full potential. Your nimbus automatically activates (if it isn’t already) and the area of your nimbus doubles; you shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) for 60 feet (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) to the next 60 feet). You can’t suppress your nimbus while Channeling your Divine Spark. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level, and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to physical damage equal to half your level. You gain the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) condition and can use the extra action each round only for [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) and [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) actions. Each time that you damage a creature with a melee Strike, you can attempt to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) that creature as a free action. These effects last for 1 minute.

---

You siphon the energies of life and death through a melee attack and into your foe. Make a melee Strike. On a hit, you cast the 1-action version of the expended spell to damage the target, in addition to the normal damage from your Strike. The target automatically gets a failure on its save (or a critical failure if your Strike was a critical hit). The spell doesn’t have the manipulate trait when cast this way.

The spell is expended with no effect if your Strike fails or hits a creature that isn’t damaged by that energy type (such as if you hit a non-undead creature with a heal spell).

---

You enter a stance that allows power to flow through you. While in this stance, whenever you [cast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) or [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) an apparition spell or vessel spell that deals energy damage, you gain a status bonus to the spell’s damage equal to the spell’s rank. 

Each time you Cast a Spell that has the [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) or [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) traits and that restores Hit Points while in this stance, the spells’ targets gain a status bonus to the initial amount of healing received equal to the spell’s rank. This bonus healing does not apply to healing over time effects (such as [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) or [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72)).

**Source** [Wake the Dead #3](/Sources.aspx?ID=212) pg. 25 --- This is the secret of chaotic magic — your foe can hardly predict and counter your moves if you yourself have no idea what will happen. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that deals acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage, roll a d6. The spell's damage type changes to the type below associated with the result of the roll, and each creature who is damaged by the spell takes the listed additional effect.
**1 (Acid):** [Sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) 1
**2 (Cold):** -10 ft. penalty to all Speeds until the end of your next turn.
**3 (Electricity):** [Flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the end of your next turn.
**4 (Fire):** [Persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) equal to the spell's level
**5 (Force):** No added effect
**6 (Sonic):** [Deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 2 rounds

You’ve learned to mimic the abilities of spellcasters by studying their flourishes and words. When you activate a magic item to generate a spell effect, attempt a Deception check. If you succeed against an onlooker’s Perception DC, to that onlooker, you appear to [Cast that Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=72) instead. Onlookers who successfully [Recognize the Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=834) realize you used a magic item, though those who later successfully [Identify the Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24) still can’t determine that the source of the effect was a magic item.

[Charmed Sleep](/Feats.aspx?ID=6868) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sprite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=774" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 47

</column>

---

When you sleep, you turn into an inanimate object a little smaller than a human’s thumb—easily overlooked and carried. Being in your Charmed Sleep counts as setting up a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) use of Deception (except that you Impersonate an object instead of a creature), it gives you a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through your disguise, and you add your level even if you’re untrained. While in your Charmed Sleep, you can be picked up and carried as easily as any small object. This effect immediately ends as soon as you wake.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Charming Liar](/Feats.aspx?ID=5132) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 253

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

Your charm allows you to win over those you lie to. When you get a critical success using the Lie action, the target’s attitude toward you improves by one step, as though you’d succeeded at using Diplomacy to Make an Impression. This works only once per conversation, and if you critically succeed against multiple targets using the same result, you choose one creature’s attitude to improve. You must be lying to impart seemingly important information, inflate your status, or ingratiate yourself, which trivial or irrelevant lies can’t achieve.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 92

**Trigger**
You take damage that would reduce you to 0 Hit Points.

</column>

---

Somehow you always escape the reaper by a hair's breadth. You avoid being knocked out or killed and remain at 1 Hit Point, but you become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) (or increase your doomed value by 1 if you were already doomed). You can't reduce or ignore the doomed condition from Cheating Death. The doomed condition from Cheating Death lasts for 10 minutes, though this doesn't affect the duration of any other doomed condition you have.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ratfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=234" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 22

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Unless specifically noted otherwise, most wands and scrolls are less than 1 foot long and can fit into a ratfolk’s Cheek Pouches_

</column>

---

Your cheeks are stretchy, and you can store up to four items of light Bulk or less in these cheek pouches. None of these items can have a dimension longer than 1 foot. As long as you have at least one item in your cheek pouches, your speech is noticeably difficult to understand. Placing an item in your cheek pouch or retrieving one is an Interact action. You can empty your mouth with a single action, causing everything you had stored in your cheek pouches to fall to the ground in your square.

<title level="2">Cheek Pouches leads to...</title>

[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

</column>

---

You have designated an ally to be you and your [companion’s](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) ward, making it your primary directive to shield them from harm. During your daily preparations, choose an ally who isn’t your united companion. While either you or your united companion are adjacent to your ward, you grant them a +1 circumstance bonus to their AC and Reflex saves. 

When your ward attempts a Reflex saving throw while adjacent to either you or your united companion, you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) as a reaction to allow your ward to roll that Reflex save twice and take the better result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.

**Special** If you have the [Defend Our Union](/Feats.aspx?ID=7351)  feat, it can also be triggered when a foe successfully Strikes your ward; if used in this way, the damage to your ward is reduced if your Strike is successful instead.

When using a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60), [lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=29), or other artificial light source to illuminate an area of [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) or darker, you use a combination of alchemical reagents, medicinal components, and colored lenses to turn that light one of seven colors, allowing you to help an ally recover from [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). You give that target an assisted recovery, but the target can be anywhere within the [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) of the light source instead of needing to be adjacent to you. Ambient bright light (like sunlight) drowns out your artificial illumination and prevents you from using Chromotherapy. The color of the light you choose determines the type of persistent damage from which you help the target recover. ##

RedYou increase blood flow to heat the body, attempting to end persistent cold damage.
OrangeYou cancel out electric charge, attempting to end persistent electricity damage.
YellowYou reduce pain and mental stress, attempting to end persistent mental damage.
GreenYou promote blood flow in a way that helps clot wounds, attempting to end persistent bleed damage.
BlueYou cool the body, attempting to end persistent fire damage.
IndigoYou render acids inert, attempting to end persistent acid damage.
VioletYou purify the body, attempting to end persistent poison damage.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 184

**Archetype** [Time Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=191)

**Prerequisites**
[Time Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3839); master in Perception

</column>

---

The flows and ebbs of time are obvious to you, as are the tangles that form when it's distorted. You're automatically aware if any creature that you observe is under the effects of the [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) or [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32) conditions. You have a general idea when you're in the vicinity of time-manipulating phenomena, though this grants you no particular insight into the specific effects of the anomaly. Particularly subtle temporal anomalies might still escape your notice, requiring a Perception check, as determined by the GM. If you're legendary in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13), whenever a creature that you can observe gains the benefits  of [_time stop_](/Spells.aspx?ID=339) or similar effects, you can observe what happens during the stopped time, though you still can't act yourself for the duration.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chronoskimmer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3847) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 186

**Archetype** [Chronoskimmer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=192)

</column>

---

You became partially unstuck from time and have learned how to manipulate your place in flow of time. When you roll initiative, you can choose one of three options: either do nothing and roll initiative normally, stabilize your timestream, or destabilize your timestream and send it into intense fluctuations. If you choose to stabilize your timestream, you don't roll initiative, and instead your initiative is equal to 10 + your initiative modifier. If you choose to destabilize your timestream, attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a success, your initiative is equal to 19 + your initiative modifier, and on a failure, your initiative is equal to 1 + your initiative modifier. Both stabilizing and destabilizing your timestream are [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effects.

 Additionally, if your initiative roll result is tied with an opponent's initiative roll, you go first. Your manipulation of time grants you access to a number of abilities, some of which require a saving throw. The DC for these abilities is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your chronoskimmer DC.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the chronoskimmer archetype.

<title level="2">Chronoskimmer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Borrow Time](/Feats.aspx?ID=3852), [Combat Premonition](/Feats.aspx?ID=3854), [Escape Timeline](/Feats.aspx?ID=3855), [Guide the Timeline](/Feats.aspx?ID=3849), [Reset the Past](/Feats.aspx?ID=3857), [Reversing Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3850), [Space-Time Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=3856), [Steal Time](/Feats.aspx?ID=3853), [Superimpose Time Duplicates](/Feats.aspx?ID=3851), [Turn Back the Clock](/Feats.aspx?ID=3848)

You know that the greatest treasures often look like refuse, and you scoff at those who throw away perfectly good scraps. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27), and you can use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) when you Subsist in a settlement.

**Special** If you have the irongut goblin heritage, increase the bonuses to +2.

Everyone has a place and a role, and as long as those roles are filled, the government functions. fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Claim Cardinal Domains](/Feats.aspx?ID=7393) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 131

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

Your dominion over the divine truths of the world increases. You can lay claim to up to three additional domains, to a total maximum of four. Your mortal form cannot easily contain such power, however—each day during your daily preparations, decide which of your domains you are currently drawing power from; you gain access to this domain for the day and can cast its domain spells as normal, while your ability to access the power of your other domains lies dormant. You learn the advanced domain spell for any domain that you have claimed with your godling abilities.

When you gain this feat, you can choose not to lay claim to one or more domains immediately, instead leaving the space open until later in your story. As long as you have one or more domains unclaimed, you can spend a Mythic Point as a single action to claim a domain, even in the heat of battle, immediately making this your active domain. This domain remains a part of your portfolio forever and cannot be changed after this point.

You can also spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to overcharge your divine power, gaining access to all the domains you have claimed for the next minute and passing this access on to your hierophant as normal. After the minute ends, you can choose which of the four domains you retain access to until your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Claim the Field](/Feats.aspx?ID=7809) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Commander" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=855" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 31

**Prerequisites**
[Plant Banner](/Feats.aspx?ID=7796)

**Requirements**
Your banner is attached to a thrown weapon.

</column>

---

You hurl your banner forward with precision, claiming the battlefield for yourself and your allies. You Plant the Banner, but you can place it at any corner within the required weapon's first range increment, rather than the corner of your square. The calculated confidence of this brash maneuver unnerves your enemies; any enemy who attempts to damage or remove your banner while it is planted in this way must succeed at a Will save against your class DC or the attempt fails. On a critical failure, the enemy is [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) for 1 round. This is an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) and mental effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 200

**Access**
You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.

</column>

---

Raised in the ancient halls of Dongun Hold or the surrounding region, you display your lineage with a clan pistol, rather than a clan dagger. You get one clan pistol of your clan for free, as it was given to you at birth. This replaces your [clan dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=13). Selling this pistol is a terrible taboo and earns you the disdain of other dwarves. You are trained with the clan pistol. In addition, when your clan pistol is visible, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus on checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) or [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) when interacting with citizens of Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or their allies.

Your [clan dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=13) can protect your allies as easily as yourself. When you use an Interact action to gain a circumstance bonus to AC from your clan dagger’s parry trait, you can grant the circumstance bonus to an adjacent ally instead of gaining it yourself. You can use multiple Interact actions to protect multiple allies, or to protect yourself and an ally. The ally benefits from the bonus to AC only when they are adjacent to you.

>
[Clawdancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5436) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 68

**Archetype** [Clawdancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=221)

**Prerequisites**
permanent unarmed claw or talon attack (such as one granted by your ancestry or a graft)

</column>

---

You've practiced the art of fighting with your natural claws, hooking them into prey and thrashing at targets surrounding you. You gain the following two actions, which let you assume specific stances to strike more effectively with your claws.

 **Claw Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=701)) **Effect** You extend the claws in your hands and focus your attention to take down single targets. The only Strikes you can make are frenzied claw unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 slashing damage, are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group, and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=619), [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719), and [versatile piercing](/Traits.aspx?ID=724) traits.

 **Talon Stance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=701)) **Effect** You sway in a loose stance that lets you sweep in wide arcs with the claws on your feet. The only Strikes you can make are spinning talon unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage, are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group, and have the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=708), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) traits. You don't need a free hand to use spinning talon strikes.

<title level="2">Clawdancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Abscission Shards](/Feats.aspx?ID=5440), [Claw and Talon Flow](/Feats.aspx?ID=5448), [Claw Snag](/Feats.aspx?ID=5437), [Dashing Pounce](/Feats.aspx?ID=5438), [Feline Dance](/Feats.aspx?ID=5445), [Hindquarter Kick](/Feats.aspx?ID=5442), [Hunting Snag](/Feats.aspx?ID=5446), [Precise Hooks](/Feats.aspx?ID=5449), [Spinning Stand](/Feats.aspx?ID=5443), [Springboard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5447), [Storm of Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=5450), [Talon Sweep](/Feats.aspx?ID=5439), [Tear Tendons](/Feats.aspx?ID=5444), [Wheeling Grab](/Feats.aspx?ID=5441)

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 24

</column>

---

Compact layers of air diffract and bend light around your body, making you appear as clear as the sky on a perfect day. You become [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) until the end of your next turn. You can Sustain the impulse. If you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300), the impulse ends after that action is completed. If you activate your kinetic aura, the impulse conceals its elements, though any special effects of your aura might give away your location.

 This impulse weakens if you use it too frequently. Using it again within 10 minutes makes you [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) instead of invisible.

---
**Level (10th)** The impulse doesn't end if you take a hostile action, but if you're invisible, you become concealed instead of invisible until the start of your next turn.

**Level (16th)** Taking a hostile action has no effect on the impulse.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 217

**Archetype** [Cleric](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=212)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You cast spells like a cleric. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the divine spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for cleric archetype spells is Wisdom, and they are divine cleric spells.

Choose a deity as you would if you were a cleric. You become bound by that deity’s anathema and can receive that deity’s divine sanctification. You become trained in Religion and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You don’t gain any other abilities from your choice of deity.

<title level="2">Cleric Dedication leads to...</title>

>
[Clever Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5041) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 204

**Prerequisites**
[Counterspell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4994); [Quick Recognition](/Feats.aspx?ID=5197)

</column>

---

You creatively apply your prepared spells to Counterspell a much wider variety of your opponents’ magic. Instead of being able to counter a foe’s spell with Counterspell only if you have that same spell prepared, you can use Counterspell as long as you have the spell the foe is casting in your spellbook. When you use Counterspell in this way, you must still expend a prepared spell; the prepared spell you expend must share a trait with the triggering spell other than concentrate, manipulate, or its tradition trait. The GM might allow you to instead use a spell that has an opposing trait or that otherwise logically would counter the triggering spell (such as using a cold or water spell to counter fireball or using clear mind to counter a fear spell).

    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Climate Adaptation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3430) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=225" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 77

**Access**
Pine leshies have access to this feat

</column>

---

Like evergreen trees, which stay healthy and vibrant from winter through summer, you too can adapt to a variety of extreme climates. You're unaffected by mild cold or heat environmental effects, and when you're in severe cold or heat, you take the effects of mild cold or heat instead (see [Table 10–13](/Rules.aspx?ID=642)). This doesn't protect you from extreme or incredible cold or heat.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cling](/Feats.aspx?ID=1428) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 45

**Requirements**
Your last action was a successful Strike.

</column>

---

You hang onto a foe to harry them into submission. If your target moves while you're hanging onto it, you can choose to move with the target. The target is released if you choose not to move with it, at the start of your next turn, or if the target [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79). Attempts to Escape from a Cling follow the rules for Escape, but use your [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) DC and end the Cling instead of the conditions normally ended by the Escape action.

**Special** You can use this action without a free hand if your preceding Strike was made with your jaws or a similar unarmed attack you could use to hang on. The GM determines which unarmed attacks apply. Hanging on in this way prevents you from using that unarmed attack.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

With a mighty blow, you send an enemy flying backward and onto the ground. Strike a foe. This Strike deals an extra die of weapon damage. If you hit and deal damage, you can automatically [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) the target, with the same benefits as the Shove action (including the critical success effect, if your Strike was a critical hit). The target then falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). This counts as two attacks when calculating your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289).

---

You can animate corpses through cunning engineering. You gain a [prototype construct companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=1600) to serve as a minion. Unlike normal construct companions, yours is a corpse animated by clockwork gears and technological prowess.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the clockwork reanimator archetype. If you retrain out of this feat, you lose the rituals learned from it.

Your unparalleled athletic skill allows you to jump impossible distances. Triple the distance you jump on a successful [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) (so you could jump 90 feet with an Athletics result of 30). When you successfully [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), use the distance jumped and distance limit for a Long Jump but don’t triple the distance.

Using fantastic acrobatic skill, you can walk for brief stretches across insubstantial surfaces. When you Stride, you can move across water, air, and solid surfaces that can hold only limited weight as if they were normal ground. If you Stride over a trap with a weight-sensitive pressure plate, you don’t trigger it. At the end of your turn, you sink, fall, break fragile surfaces, or trigger traps as normal for your current location.

Your growing link to cloud dragons has granted you the ability to walk on clouds. Once per hour, you can cast [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6) on yourself as an innate arcane spell, but only to walk on clouds or fog.

The following archetype feats are for the dragon disciple archetype. You must take the Dragon Disciple Dedication feat before selecting any of these feats, and you must select cloud dragon (which is associated with the electricity energy type) as the type of dragon you've studied. The feats below are dragon disciple archetype feats. By studying the ruins (see the AP for full details), you gain access to the dragon disciple archetype and to these feats

 If you have the [draconic sorcerer](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=5) bloodline, you must choose cloud dragon as your dragon type. This choice affects the [_dragon breath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=499) and [_dragon claws_](/Spells.aspx?ID=500) bloodline spells and several of the feats below.

**Related Feats**: [Deflecting Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=3408), [Mighty Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=3409), [Shape of the Cloud Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=3407)

[Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Vampire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3545)

</column>

---

You bind your spirit to a coffin filled with soil of your homeland, making it a place of recovery. If you rest inside your coffin for 10 minutes, you regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier × half your level. You can still be healed in other ways during that time, though you're [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and therefore unable to heal yourself. The GM might allow you to [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) while resting, depending on whether it's a type of Refocusing you can achieve while you slumber.

 If you would be destroyed, you instead remain near death. This doesn't change your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) or [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) value, and you remain unconscious. After 1 hour, you're destroyed. If returned to your coffin before that hour is up, you avoid destruction; if you spend 1 hour resting in your coffin, you regain 1 HP and lose the dying and wounded conditions. You can't be healed in any other way when near death.

 Your coffin can't heal you if you're staked through the chest. You can be staked only if unconscious, and it takes three actions. You lose all benefits of this feat if your coffin is destroyed or the soil is lost. You must procure a new coffin and fill it with soil of your homeland to restore the feat's function.

<title level="2">Coffin Bound leads to...</title>
[Mist Escape](/Feats.aspx?ID=3555)

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Trigger**
An enemy's Strike against you is a critical hit.

</column>

---

You collapse into a pile of bones, mitigating the worst of the damage you would have taken, and the triggering attack deals only the amount it would deal on a hit (typically full damage instead of double damage). Any other effects caused by a critical hit still occur. While collapsed, you're [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and can't act except to Stand, which re-forms you into a skeleton in a standing position.

>
[Collapse Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=3051) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Modification" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=410" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 25

**Prerequisites**
[armor innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=1)

**Requirements**
You are wearing your armor innovation, or holding it in both hands in its compact form (see text).

</column>

---

You've modified your armor innovation to collapse into a more compact form so you can don or remove it in an instant. If you’re wearing your innovation when you Collapse your Armor, you remove it instantly, and it compresses into its compact form, after which it latches onto your body, typically by attaching to a belt, bandoleer, or other convenient carrying surface as a nondescript satchel. If your armor is stowed and carried on your person in its compact form when you take this action, it unfolds back into its armor form onto your body.

 In compact form, your armor innovation is easier to carry, with a Bulk 1 lower than the Bulk listed for it, to a minimum of light Bulk (carried armor normally has a Bulk 1 higher than listed in the armor entry).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Modification" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=410" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 25

**Prerequisites**
[construct innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

You've modified your construct companion and built it out of light materials, enabling you to collapse it into a carrying case or other compact and innocuous form. Either your construct or you (if you're adjacent to it) can Collapse your Construct to turn it into its compact form or back into its normal form.

 In compact form, your construct can't act but is easily carried, with a Bulk of 2 if it's Small, 4 if it's Medium, or 8 if it's Large. The compact form has wheels, so you can easily drag it behind you at half your Speed (rather than the usual slower Speed for dragging).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Collapse Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=3244) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 133

**Archetype** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=118)

**Prerequisites**
[Demolitionist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3240)

**Trigger**
A creature moves into the bombs' splash area.

**Requirements**
You're within 30 feet of an area where you rigged bombs on a wall, cliff face, or similar vertical surface with Set Explosives or Demolition Charge.

</column>

---

You detonate the required bombs in order to bring a wall down on a creature. If your bombs deal enough damage to reduce the wall's Hit Points below its Broken Threshold, the wall partially collapses on the creature. The creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to the damage dealt to the wall ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; the DC for this save is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher). On a failure, they must spend an Interact action to dig themselves out of the collapse, and on a critical failure, they must spend 2 Interact actions to do so.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 187

**Archetype** [Chronoskimmer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=192)

**Prerequisites**
[Chronoskimmer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3847)

</column>

---

By narrowing your sense of the future, you can improve that of your allies. When you roll initiative, instead of stabilizing or destabilizing your own timestream, you can grant your allies a flash of insight into their future. Choose two allies. Those allies roll their initiative roll twice and take the better result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. You roll your initiative roll twice and take the worse result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect. The two effects are tied together: if you would avoid the misfortune effect for any reason, or if any of your allies would negate their fortune effect, your Combat Premonition does nothing.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 112 --- You use a performer's cold reading techniques, aura reading, and other tricks to discover your foe's strengths and weaknesses. The GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) check for you against the [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) DC (whichever is higher) of an enemy of your choice who is engaged in combat and isn't [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from you, [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from you, or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by you. The GM might apply a penalty for the distance between you and the enemy. The enemy is then temporarily immune to your Combat Reading for 1 day. **Critical Success** The GM chooses and tells you two of the following pieces of information about the enemy: which of the enemy's weaknesses is highest, which of the enemy's saving throws has the lowest modifier, one immunity the enemy has, or which of the enemy's resistances is highest. In the event of a tie, the GM should pick one at random.
**Success** The GM chooses one piece of information from the above list to tell you about the enemy.
**Critical Failure** The GM gives you false information (the GM makes up the information).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Additive 2" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=4" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 78

**Frequency**
once per round

**Trigger**
You use Quick Alchemy to craft an alchemical item that has the elixir trait and is at least 2 levels lower than your advanced alchemy level.

</column>

---

You’ve discovered how to mix two elixirs into a single hybrid concoction. You can spend 2 additional batches of infused reagents to add a second elixir to the one you’re crafting. The second elixir must also be at least 2 levels lower than your advanced alchemy level, and the combination elixir is an alchemical item two levels higher than the higher of the two elixirs’ levels. When this combination elixir is consumed, both the constituent elixirs take effect. For example, you can combine two [elixirs of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91) to create a combined elixir that heals twice the normal amount, or you can combine a [lesser darkvision elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=89) with a [lesser eagle-eye elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=90) to both gain darkvision and find secret doors.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 68

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The Combined Form tanuki feat overrides the normal restrictions that a target can only be under the effect of one polymorph effect at a time._

**Frequency**
Once per hour

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet uses a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect.

</column>

---

Cooperation and coordination are the secrets to getting by in tanuki society. When the triggering ally transforms, you Stride to their square and join shape with them, melding into their transformation. While you’re melded in this way, you grant them the effects of either a 2nd- or 4th‑rank [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1514) spell as well as temporary Hit Points equal to your level; if their [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect would normally grant them temporary Hit Points, you increase the amount by your level instead. While you’re melded, you can’t be separately targeted and you can’t act except to speak or to use Change Shape to exit the Combined Form, which ends the effects of enlarge on your ally and removes any remaining temporary Hit Points they received from this ability at the time. If the triggering ally becomes [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or the triggering polymorph effect ends, you automatically exit the Combined Form.

You open yourself to attacks so you can respond in turn. Until your rage ends, you are flat-footed, and damage rolls against you gain a +2 circumstance bonus. </title>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />

**Prerequisites**
[World Rouser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9376)

**Requirements**
Your waking world is active.

</column>

---

A willing ally on the ground in your waking world is swaddled in earth. For each source of [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) it is taking, the creature can immediately attempt a [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to recover, with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance. While [swallowed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77), the creature becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) and cannot be targeted or affected by any new effects (ongoing effects, such as [afflictions](/Rules.aspx?ID=2765) or persistent damage, continue to affect it as normal). At the start of your next turn, the creature regains 6d8 Hit Points and emerges in its previous location. If another creature is in that location, it is pushed to the nearest available space. The target creature then becomes temporarily immune to this ability until your next daily preparations.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 166

**Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=54)

**Prerequisites**
[Celebrity Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1931)

</column>

---

You command the attention of all around you with style, ensuring their gaze falls only upon you until the end of your next turn. When creatures within 30 feet of you attempt saving throws against other [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) effects, they use the outcome for one degree of success better than the result they rolled. An enemy within the area attempting to use a visual effect that involves focusing its attention on a particular creature (such as a [medusa's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297) Focus Gaze) must succeed at a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, in order to target any creature except you. Allies in the area can attempt to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) even if they don't have cover, as you are continually providing a distraction.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 21 --- You grasp the animating force within an elemental creature and bend it to your will. Choose a trait matching one of your kinetic elements and target an [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) creature within 30 feet that has the chosen trait. The elemental becomes [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) by you if its level is equal to or lower than your level — 3, or [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for as long as you Sustain the effect if its level is equal to your level — 2 or higher. It can attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC to resist being controlled by you or to end the slowed effect. If the target is already under someone else's command, it can't be slowed by this ability, and the controlling creature also rolls a saving throw, with the elemental using the better result. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** The elemental creature is controlled or slowed as long as you Sustain the impulse, up to 1 minute. This effect ends if you or an ally attacks the elemental.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 hour.

If given no commands, undead minions use no actions except to defend themselves or to escape obvious harm. If left unattended for at least 1 minute, mindless undead minions don’t act, and intelligent ones act as they please. You can’t have more than four undead minions at a time.

    right="Feat 1"

>
[Commander's Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7793) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Commander" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=855" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 30

</column>

---

You gain the service of a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2113). You can affix your banner to your companion's saddle, barding, or a simple harness, determining the effects of your commander's banner and other abilities that use your banner from your companion's space, even if you are not currently riding your companion. A companion granted by this feat always counts as one of your squadmates and does not count against your maximum number of squadmates.

**Special** When you use [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to command the companion granted by this feat, it gains a reaction it can  only use in response to your tactics. This reaction is lost if it  is not used by the end of your turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Communal Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5135) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 253

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You can have other PCs help you Craft an item, under your direction. A helper PC rolls a check with a skill in which they’re trained. The skill must be Crafting or another skill relevant to the item, as determined by the GM. For example, a PC might use Religion to help you Craft an item with the divine trait or Warfare Lore to help you Craft a weapon. Your roll still determines whether you successfully create the item. Any helper’s roll contributes toward reducing the cost of raw materials using the numbers from the Earn Income table on page 229; this uses the ally PC’s proficiency rank in the skill and their level – 1 for their level.

Helping PCs must accompany you throughout the Craft activity (preventing them from pursuing other downtime activities) or the benefit is lost. The GM might determine that only a certain number of PCs can help depending on the circumstances.

Communal Crafting also allows you to take the role of a helper when someone else is crafting, provided they accept your help.

Stories are an experience meant to be shared as a group. When you Spin a Tale, you can designate up to six non-[minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) allies as the heroes of your story. Each hero, once during the tale, can continue the story in your stead by spending an action to Spin the Tale; if they do, the story continues for another round, as if you had Spun the Tale at the start of your turn. This could allow the story to continue for up to 6 additional rounds, if all possible allies Spin the Tale, though you can continue to Spin the Tale on your own as normal.

<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 101, [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 210

</column>

---

Hiding your gestures and incantations within other speech and movement, you attempt to conceal the fact that you are Casting a Spell. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, attempt a Stealth check against one or more observers’ Perception DCs; if the spell has verbal components, you must also attempt a Deception check against the observers’ Perception DC. If you succeed at your check (or checks) against an observer’s DC, that observer doesn’t notice you’re casting a spell, even though material, somatic, and verbal components are usually noticeable and spells normally have sensory manifestations that would make spellcasting obvious to those nearby.

 This ability hides only the spell’s spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects, so an observer might still see a ray streak out from you or see you vanish into thin air.

Rather than hide an object somewhere the inspectors won't search, you're skilled at keeping the object on the move so it's never where they look. Because you know your mind is superior, you scoff at anyone who would alter your mental state—but this hubris gets the better of you when you're wrong. If you succeed at a save against a mental effect, you critically succeed instead; similarly, if you fail at a save against a mental effect, you critically fail instead.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121)

**Prerequisites**
[Sniping Duo Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3258)

</column>

---

You and your spotter combine your efforts to bring down your target. If you and your spotter both use the Ready activity to make a Strike against the same opponent and choose the same trigger for the readied action, resolve your attacks at the same time. Each of you can use the higher of the two attack rolls for your Strikes, each using your own modifier; this is a fortune effect. If both attacks are successful, total the damage for both attacks for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Infernal Pactbreaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=398)

**Prerequisites**
[Infernal Pactbreaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9488)

</column>

---

With a quick flourish, you draw together runes and legal bindings to condemn a creature’s soul and bring it to justice. Select a creature within 30 feet of you; that creature must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result, the target is then temporarily immune to your Condemn Soul for 1 day.

<column gap="tiny">

**Success** The target is unaffected.

**Failure** Your condemnation frays the fabric of the target’s soul. The target gains weakness to fire and spirit damage equal to half your level for 1 minute. Only you can trigger this weakness.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but any creature can trigger the creature’s weakness.

</column>

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Conductive Sphere](/Feats.aspx?ID=4259) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Electricity" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=56" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 31

</column>

---

A floating metal ball forms in a space within 30 feet, flashing with electricity. It can't be targeted or damaged. Any of your allies adjacent to it gain resistance to electricity equal to your level and add the [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=303) rune to all their Strikes with metal objects. The sphere lasts until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain it up to 1 minute.

 When you conjure the sphere and the first time you Sustain the impulse on subsequent rounds, you can either have it [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to 20 feet or deal 1d12 electricity damage to an adjacent creature with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC.

---
**Level (+3)** The damage dealt by the sphere increases by 1d12.

You use the unstable energy of your [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566) to manipulate the most basic of divine magic. You cast a 3-action [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) or [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552) spell, expending the slot as normal.     right="Feat 6"

>
[Confounding Image](/Feats.aspx?ID=3377) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_mirror image_](/Spells.aspx?ID=197)

</column>

---

When you cast _mirror image_, you can modify its duration to be sustained up to 1 minute and modify its range to 30 feet. If you do, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: You create an illusory duplicate of yourself that appears in an unoccupied square within range. The image takes up space and has a reach of 5 feet, and your allies can flank with the image. It doesn't have any other attributes a creature would normally have other than an AC equal to your spell DC and saving throw modifiers equal to your spell DC – 10. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, or if you ever move more than 30 feet from it, the spell ends. Creatures can move through its space without hindrance. When you Sustain the Spell, you can move the image to an unoccupied square within range.

---

Though you might not worship [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=278) or other devils, you've studied enough of Hell to call forth a brief burst of its fire. Each creature in a 15-foot burst within 120 feet takes 9d6 fire damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save against your spell DC. This fire damage ignores an amount of fire resistance equal to your level, but not immunity to fire. A creature that fails its save also has its soul set aflame, taking 2d6 [persistent spirit damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) (or 4d6 persistent spirit damage on a critical failure). At 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the initial fire damage increases by 2d6.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 62 **Requirements** You must be pursuing at least two leads. --- Ephemeral connections between people, places, and concepts are invisible to most, but seeing them is your stock and trade. You spend 10 minutes considering two different leads you're [pursuing](/Actions.aspx?ID=544). You then attempt a check to investigate how connected the two are. Unless the GM determines otherwise, this is a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check if they're both items or a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check for other combinations of leads. If any subjects are creatures, this check usually uses the highest DC among their [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) and Will DCs. If no subjects are creatures, but at least one is an item, the DC is usually a hard DC for the level of the highest-level item. If neither case applies, the DC is usually a hard expert or hard master DC (22 or 32). Once you try to Connect the Dots between two particular leads, you can never try to Connect the Dots between those same leads again unless the GM allows it after you've learned a substantial amount of new information. **Critical Success** The GM tells you how connected the two leads are to one another: highly connected, somewhat connected, tangentially connected, or not connected. The GM also tells you one specific way in which they're connected, if they are.
**Success** As critical success, but the GM doesn't tell you a specific connection.
**Failure** Your results are inconclusive.
**Critical Failure** You misconstrue the information. As success, but the GM provides an incorrect degree of connection.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 109 --- Ephemeral connections between people, places, and concepts are invisible to most, but seeing them is your stock and trade. Choose an ally and a non-allied creature. You must be able to see both of them. You briefly study the way they both move and attempt a Perception check against the higher of the non-allied creature's [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC or Will DC. Both targets are then temporarily immune to Connect the Dots for 10 minutes. **Critical Success** You spot a way for your ally to take advantage of the other target's flaws and let them know about it. Your ally gains your [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=2811) investigation bonus as a circumstance bonus to all its Strikes or skill checks against the creature until the start of your next turn.
**Success** As critical success, but your ally gains the bonus only for their next Strike or skill check against the creature.
**Failure** You fail to make a connection.
**Critical Failure** You misconstrue a vital piece of information, which temporarily disconcerts you. You are [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) until the end of your next turn.

You have social connections you can leverage to trade favors or meet important people. When you’re in an area with connections (typically a settlement where you’ve spent downtime building connections, or possibly another area in the same nation), you can attempt a Society check to arrange a meeting with an important political figure or ask for a favor in exchange for a later favor of your contact’s choice. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conrasu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=343" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 108

</column>

---

You have learned about your history and your people from shapers. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) and [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also become trained in [Conrasu Lore](/Traits.aspx?ID=343).

You have taken it upon yourself to learn the ways of combat to aid with your tasks, perhaps in a role as a corrector. You are trained with the [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=75), [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=20), [longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=6), [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31), [shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=77), and [spear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=10). You also gain access to all uncommon [conrasu](/Traits.aspx?ID=343) weapons. For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial conrasu weapons are simple weapons and advanced conrasu weapons are martial weapons.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 84

**Prerequisites**
ability to cast focus spells, [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You infuse a spell with the power of your faith, consecrating it. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that targets a single [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), you can expend a Focus Point, channeling the power of your focus spells into the primary spell. If you do, the spell you cast deals additional good or positive damage (your choice) equal to the level of your focus spells. As normal for additional damage, this additional damage is doubled if the spell cast requires an attack roll and the result of the attack roll is a critical hit, or if the spell cast requires a saving throw and the result of the saving throw is a critical failure.
